text:
Vancouver led 2-0 early in the second period, and by every measure of how the game was played, it should not have been close. Linus Karlsson scored on a 3% slap shot late in the first, and Elias Pettersson added a power-play goal at 4:35 of the second. Tampa Bay had been out-chancing the Canucks the whole time, 1.44 to 0.67 in expected goals in the first period alone.

The comeback took less than seven minutes to start. Nikita Kucherov scored on the power play at 6:30, then again at 11:23 on a snap shot to tie it at 2. Jake Guentzel put TBL ahead 3-2 at 2:04 of the third, and Pontus Holmberg sealed it at 15:57 with an unassisted wrist shot. Kucherov finished with two goals and seven shots on goal, and the Lightning's top line of Kucherov, Point and Guentzel dominated at even strength. Brayden Point had two assists, and TBL out-chanced VAN 2.48 to 0.07 in expected goals with him on the ice.

The totals show how lopsided it was: 73 shot attempts to 51, 35 shots on goal to 14, and expected goals of 4.71 to 1.79. TBL deserved to win 82% of the time. Kevin Lankinen faced 35 shots for VAN and allowed 4 goals against 3.83 expected, so he did not cost his team the game. The Canucks simply got their two goals and then spent the rest of the night chasing a team that kept creating the better chances.
